question: Mohiniyattam dance emotes a play through dancing and singing where the song is customarily in which of the following languages?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Manipravala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Mohiniattam** stands apart from all other Indian dance genres because of its captivating grace.
 
• Mohiniattam is only a couple of centuries old in its current shape. Before reaching its current state, the dance form underwent stylistic transformations.
 
• Traditions never remain static; they change over time as a result of shifting aesthetic and social tastes. Female artists do Mohiniattam, a solo performance.
 
• The song is generally in **Manipravala**, which is a **blend of Sanskrit and Malayalam**, and the dance emotes a play through dancing and singing. The recitation is also performed in Carnatic music style, either by the dancer or by the vocalist. 
 
• **Manipravalami **is a South Indian macaronic language documented in some texts. It is a hybrid language that blends Sanskrit vocabulary with Tamil morpho-syntax and is commonly written in the Grantha script.
 
• However, the Sanskrit text Lilatilakam, written in the 14th century, claims that Manipravalam is a hybrid of Tamil and Sanskrit.
